definitions: A government formed by a coalition of two or more political parties, typically when no single party has achieved an overall majority in a general election.
A cabinet of a parliamentary government in which several political parties cooperate, reducing the dominance of any one party within that coalition.
examples: The country was governed by a coalition government for five years.
Forming a coalition government can be a complex process.
The stability of a coalition government often depends on the agreement between its constituent parties.
